title: Choose the visual world for the study site
question: Fresh hand, steered to modern and fun to learn from. The roll assigned the Flash-Card Deck.

options.label: Flash-Card Deck
options.lineage: Revision flash cards and the decks students make before exams
options.thesis: Every idea is a card you can hold, flip, and collect; lessons read like a deck you are working through.
options.viewport: A lesson column on a soft periwinkle ground; definitions and checks sit as coloured cards beside it, with a fanned deck showing the six lessons and how many you have collected.
options.risk: Can tip into a kids' quiz app if the cards get bouncy or the type gets cute.

raised.raise: Each lecture owns one full-strength hue, carried by its tab, its deck, and its cards, so you always know which lecture you are in.
In a check, every answer stays visible; the one you pick lifts forward and the rest stay put.
Colour stays out of the running text: it lives on cards, tabs, and highlights, never behind a paragraph.

options.label: Highlighter Desk
options.lineage: A student's desk the night before an exam: highlighters, sticky notes, index tabs
options.thesis: The page is your own study notes: key words highlighted, definitions on sticky notes, lessons on index tabs.
options.viewport: A clean white lesson with key terms swiped in neon, a sticky-note definition in the margin, and coloured index tabs down the side for the six lessons.
options.risk: Very familiar from study-with-me videos, so it can feel like a theme rather than ours.

options.label: Tabbed Binder Boards
options.thesis: Each lecture is a coloured divider; the whole course shows as a stepped tab rail down the edge.
options.viewport: An orange divider board for Lecture 1 with a milky reading leaf on top and a tab rail down the right edge, one tab per lecture.
options.case: Very clear wayfinding and bold colour; less playful than cards, and the acetate layering is fussy on phones.
options.risk: Can read as retro office supplies.

options.label: Struck Cathode
options.thesis: Every option glows as a ghost; the chosen one strikes forward.
options.viewport: Glowing numerals over a dark mesh.
options.case: Technical and dark; the opposite of the steer.
options.kept: Every answer stays visible; the chosen one lifts forward.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: Quiet white pages with a thin pastel fringe.
options.viewport: Wide white margins with a mint-rose-violet fringe.
options.case: Calm and readable, but not fun and unrelated to the course.
options.kept: Colour stays out of the running text.

options.label: Console Menu Void
options.thesis: Lectures as glowing towers in a dark void.
options.case: Fun for a home screen, hard to read lessons in.
options.risk: Heavy WebGL for a reading site.
options.kept: Finishing something should feel like it rises and lights up.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Annotations pinned to a strut network.
options.viewport: A force diagram with leader-line labels.
options.case: Engineering-heavy, which you asked to avoid.
options.kept: Figure labels sit on leader lines right next to what they explain.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets over a zone ramp.
options.case: Clever but not fun or familiar to students.
options.kept: Wrong answers are marked by shape as well as colour, so they read without colour.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean documentation site, like the best course and docs sites, done with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of lectures and lessons, a centred article column, an on-this-page list on the right.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other docs site by design.
